Commentary.Commentary: Around 28 overs left in the day. Can Bangladesh make any impression with the ball? How much can New Zealand score? At least a 100, one would imagine. Their reply is on the way...

Poor start from New Zealand, especially after electing to field. They sprayed the ball all over the pitch and Tamim took full toll. However, after Lunch, they quickly adjusted their lengths and were rewarded. From 121/1, the visitors have collapsed to 234. Neil Wagner took 5 wickets, meaning he now has 9 scalps in his last 2 innings, after taking a 4-fer against Sri Lanka in Christchurch. Southee, after enduring a torrid morning, finished with a 3-fer.

Remember the story of the 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s and the 2000s? Asian team touring overseas, getting peppered with short stuff and surrendering meekly. Something similar has happened here. Bangladesh have shown no determination and lost 8 out of the 10 wickets to short stuff. No resistance to temptation in playing a pull shot and no control in any of the pull or hook shots played. Really sad, given that they have improved so well over the last few months.

That did not take long, did it? Just 4 overs to be precise, to take the remaining 3 wickets. New Zealand have just gotten all over Bangladesh like a rash. Save aside Tamim's 126, there is nothing much to write about the batting.

OUT! No threats to the 5-fer! Wagner has picked it up! And no prizes for guessing, it is the short ball that has done the trick once more. A short of a length ball at the hips, Liton connects his pull really well but the ball flies straight to Trent Boult at deep fine leg who is positioned exactly for that. He takes a good catch to his left and at a good height. Bangladesh who were 147/2 at one stage have been bowled out for 234. They will be disappointed, on the other hand, the Kiwis will be ecstatic with the way the day has turned out. Neil Wagner, as expected, receives the ball and leads his teammates on the way out.
Short of a length delivery outside leg, Liton Das lets it go.
Ebadot Hossain is the last man to the crease.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Southee finally goes for the yorker and finishes off Ahmed. That moving ball was too good for the number 10 bat. Nice and full at the base of off stump, Khaled did not read the line of that ball and misses it. The timber is disturbed and the visitors have lost their ninth wicket. Southee picks up his third wicket. The 5-fer of Wagner is under threat.
Bouncer! Outside off and Khaled lets it go outside off by swaying away from the line.
Huge swipe and miss! A length ball outside off and slight shape away, Ahmed goes for the huge hit over wide long on but fails to connect.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.

Short one outside off, Liton guides it to third man where Latham stops the ball with a diving effort. The batsmen want two but there is a slight hesitation and in the end, they do not get the second run. The tail-ender is on strike now.
Bouncer on the off stump line, Das looked to pull it but the ball bounces a bit more and beats the bat.
Play and a miss! Short of a length ball on middle, Ahmed looked to get outside the line and defend but failed to put bat on ball.
Short of a length and pulled away through square leg for a single by Liton.
Length ball outside off, pushed towards point.
Slower ball on the leg stump line, defended watchfully by Das.

DROPPED and FOUR! That would have been a brilliant catch had it been taken. A short of a length ball aimed at the body, Liton gets inside the line and pulls it fine. The ball goes flat and towards Boult at fine leg who dives to his right to take that. It does not stick and pops out before rolling into the ropes. Good effort but hard luck for Trent.

In the air... and lands in no man's land. A short ball from Wagner, Liton makes room and tries to cut it away. The ball gets big on him and hits him high on the bat before flying towards mid off. There is no one there to take that ball and the batsmen complete an easy couple.
Another bouncer from Southee, Ahmed ducks under it and loses balance in the end.
Khaled Ahmed walks in at number 10.

OUT! Unbelievable! Another one falls to the short ball. A bouncer on middle from Southee, Jayed makes room and tries to ramp it like he did in the first ball of this over. This time though he just gets an edge. Watling takes an easy catch behind and Bangladesh have lost their eighth. On a tough day, Southee has finally picked up his second wicket. This is BJ Watling's 200th dismissal as a wicket-keeper for the Kiwis.
Put on a length at the hips, Liton manages to turn it around to deep fine leg and gets to the other end.
A bouncer down the leg side, left alone by the batsman.
Another short one outside off, Liton pats it with a flat bat towards the vacant long on region. It is a long chase for de Grandhomme who comes around from mid-wicket to stop that at 2 runs.

What was that! A short ball on middle and leg, aimed almost at the batsman's ribs. Abu makes room and gets under the ball as if to duck before he puts his bat up there and ramps the ball over the keeper's head. The ball is not well timed. Boult comes around from fine leg and stops the ball for a single.
Tim Southee to bowl from the other end.
A defensive stroke off the back foot from Das to end the over.
FOUR! Smashed! Das has met fire with fire there. A short of a length ball once more, this time on middle, Liton makes room and pulls it hard away through mid-wicket for a boundary.

This time the short ball is well aimed at the chest and shoulder, Abu somehow gets the ball away wide of short fine leg for a single. It was in the air for a bit but somehow went away from the fielder.
Starts off with a short one, Jayed manages to make room and then defend the ball.
We are back for the final session of play. Neil Wagner to continue with his over, which has four balls left. Abu Jayed, who joins Liton Das in the middle will take strike.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

217 in 2 sessions? Wow. Well done, Bangladesh. Wait. 217/7? Same old story. The Asian tigers have not quite been able to curb their instincts and had it not been for Tamim's heroic knock, New Zealand would have been batting by now. They would hope to do so soon, after Tea given that they are into the tail. Join us back at 4 pm local (0300 GMT).

Short was the term for New Zealand. They unleashed Neil Wagner and he kept on banging it in short at the Bangladeshi batsmen. None of them were able to curtail their shots and all the dismissals in the second session have been to short stuff. Wagner, not surprisingly, has taken 4 of the tourists' scalps and is looking good for a 5-fer.

New Zealand's session. 5 wickets picked up in 27.2 overs for the cost of 95 runs. It has been an incredible couple of sessions of Test cricket with the opening belonging to the visiting side through some superlative batting while the second saw the home side 'bounce' back.

OUT! Wagner has done it again. The short stuff is working like magic and Neil has picked up his fourth. A short of a length ball on the hips and Mehidy tries to uncomfortably fend it on the leg side. The ball hits him high on the bat and goes in the air towards short leg where Nicholls takes a good, low catch. That wicket is also the last bit of action in the second session. TEA ON DAY 1. The visitors have lost their path from a good position. Wagner is pumped up and so is his team. They have picked up 5 wickets in this session after just 2 in the opening one.

SIX! That was not in control but it goes all the way. A short of a length ball on middle and leg, Mehidy swivels and pulls it away fine on the leg side for a maximum. Trent Boult at deep fine leg was interested for a bit but the ball went well away from him.
Full and around middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full again, this time with a bit of lesser pace, driven straight to cover.
A bit of extra flight outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and around off, driven straight to cover.
Floated around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Goes back to short of a length does Wagner, this time outside leg. Mehidy shoulders arms and lets the ball go.
FOUR! What a way to get off the mark by Mehidy. A length ball outside off, Hasan just opens the face of the bat and times it away wide of point beautifully for a boundary.
This one is a bouncer on middle and leg, Hasan ducks under it and lets it go.
A short of length ball aimed at the hips to welcome the new batsman, Mehidy fends it awkwardly towards the short fine leg fielder.

OUT! That is poor cricket from Bangladesh! Nothing but poor cricket. 10 minutes left to the break and absolutely unnecessary. A short ball on middle, Mahmudullah looks to pull it but gets a top edge as the ball bounces a little bit extra. Goes high in the air and towards fine leg where Boult comes in a bit, settles under the ball and takes it easily. That is another one down for the Tigers, and an important wicket just before a break. Mehidy Hasan walks in next to bat.
Continues with the short barrage, Mahmudullah ducks under this one on middle.

Superb effort from Kane Williamson. Outside off, Das guides it towards gully but the Kiwi skipper throws himself to his left to stop the ball.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
There comes the short stuff straightaway. Banged in short around middle, Das rises with the bounce but fends it down in an uncomfortable manner to the off side.
Neil Wagner is back on. Time for a 'short' burst before Tea. 12-3-25-2 so far.

Too full again, driven straight to cover this time.

Todd Astle returns. 2-0-4-0 so far.

OUT! Caught at gully! Tamim departs. Change of angle does the trick. De Grandhomme bowls this on a short length from around the wicket, angling it in, Iqbal tries to hit it through the off side but is cramped for room. He gets an outside edge which goes straight to Kane Williamson at gully. Cannot keep it down either, so it goes right into the bread basket of the Kiwi skipper. They check for the overstepping but replays show that de Grandhomme is fine. Big wicket. End of a fine innings from Tamim - 126 from 128 balls - but has he opened the door for New Zealand?

IN THE AIR... SAFE! Rash, very rash from Tamim. It is a full ball on middle and he looks to clamp it over mid on. But he skies it very high in the air and mid on starts to run back for the catch. Luckily for the batsman, it is far from the fielder who cannot reach it even with a dive. Two runs taken. The Drinks break has just ended but won't be surprised if someone comes out with a bottle of drinks or some gloves with a message for Tamim. Calm down, son!
FOUR! Wow. That is really impressive. A length ball on middle, Tamim walks across and lofts it over mid on!

DRINKS BREAK. As expected, the Kiwis have come roaring back after Lunch. 2 wickets in 13 overs for 48 runs. It is all coming down to Tamim vs New Zealand and the Prince of Chattogram is doing his best to keep the Black Caps at bay. But one cannot help but feeling that his wicket might just set the cat free amongst the pigeons. Colin de Grandhomme into the attack. 6-0-19-0 so far.
Outside off, another one moves away after pitching, almost taking the outside edge as Mahmudullah looks to defend.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.

Teases the batsman outside off, draws him into the poke and then gets it away from him, beating the outside edge.
Fuller in length, outside off, Mahmudullah feels for it but misses.

Quick single taken. Around off, on a good length, Tamim hops and pushes it in front of cover and sets off for a quick single. The fielder comes running in and has an underarm shy at the keeper's end but misses. Mahmudullah was in anyways.
Trent Boult back for another spell. 8-0-46-1 so far.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total. 15 from the over.
FOUR! BLAST! Looks like Tamim has had enough of these short pitched deliveries. Takes this one on and pulls it between deep mid-wicket and fine leg.
FOUR! Streaky. Short and down the leg side, Tamim swivels and looks to pull. The ball takes the inside edge and goes past the keeper to the fine leg fence!
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

DROPPED, SIX! Tough chance but half a chance. A short ball, around middle, Tamim swivels and goes for the pull. He middles it pretty well but the height is not that great. Neil Wagner runs to his right from long leg, leaps but gets fingertips to it as the ball bursts through.
Around off, Tamim is in the air, trying to fend that, getting it off the face of the bat and JUST eluding short leg.
On a good length around middle, angling away, Mahmudullah hops, skips and jumps, pushing it towards the off side.

Mahmudullah, the skipper, walks in at number 6, replacing Sarkar. None better than the captain to provide a stand.

OUT! Left alone, trying to leave it alone but gloved behind! The wickets continue to tumble and Tamim is quickly running out partners now. 4 down and not too many batsmen to come. That flying start in the first session is beginning to be put in the forgotten pages of history now. Short of a length, around off, angling away, Sarkar looks to leave it alone, trying to get his hands out of the way. But the ball keeps on climbing, takes the glove and deflects to the keeper! Frustration continues to mount for Bangladesh as they now look keenly at Tamim's response. The Kiwis are cunningly trying to isolate him.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.

FOUR! There it is! 9th Test ton for Tamim Iqbal, first vs New Zealand! Also, a ton in this format after 25 innings, with the last one being in October 2016, against England in Dhaka! he has literally demolished this Kiwi attack. 102 in a team's score of 144. Wow. Gets to the landmark with a brilliant pull through mid-wicket. Raises his arms to the crowd and the dressing room. Now, for some composure.
A short ball, around middle, TI whips it but straight onto the helmet of short leg! Jeez, that would have hurt.

OOPS! Almost dismissed on 93! That would have been a really silly way to get out. A short ball, around middle, Tamim ducks but his bat hangs in the air like a periscope. The ball takes the top edge and lobs in the air but does not carry to BJ Watling behind! Poor technique, lucky to get away.
FOUR! FANTASTIC! Tamim is into the 90s! This is as good a shot as any! Overpitched outside off, Iqbal leans and drives it through the covers. Moves to 93...

Not the greatest bit of bowling from the Kiwis. After electing to bowl on what looks like a green surface, they have sprayed the ball all around the park. Expect them to come back hard in the second session.

Enthralling session of cricket. More than 100 runs scored at more than 4 an over. Tamim Iqbal has been the centre of attraction, scoring 70 percent of the runs. He has looked solid and put behind him the disappointment of the ODIs.

FOUR! FOURTH BOUNDARY OF THE OVER! This is the pair of Trent Boult and Tim Southee bowling but Tamim is taking them to the cleaners. Outside off, on a length, Iqbal flays it through point.
Around off, defended solidly.

FOUR! Three in a row! 26TH TEST FIFTY FOR TAMIM, in just 37 balls! A total flop in the one-dayers, he has embraced this Test with a warm hug. Full and outside off, Iqbal leans and drives it through the covers!
FOUR! That is a bad ball. Half volley around middle, Tamim flicks it through mid-wicket and the ball races away!
FOUR! CLASSY! Full and wide outside off, swinging away, Tamim leans into the shot and drives it through the covers!
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! CARESSED! That is a lovely shot. The ball is full and swings in a great deal. But Tamim covers the line and the movement beautifully and drives it through mid on!
A bouncer on middle, Tamim ducks.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, Mominul plays inside the line and is beaten.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, another outswinger, Mominul looks to drive but gets an outside edge which does not carry to second slip.
Mominul Haque walks in at number 3, replacing Shadman Islam.

OUT! That is a real peach. The outswinger takes the first wicket. What a brilliant nut from Boult. This is pitched on a fuller length around off, but Shadman does not cover the line at all. He looks to push it to the leg side but the ball swings away and hits the base of off stump. It has taken 10 overs but the Kiwis have eventually struck.
FOUR! The runs continue to flow. Half volley outside off, Shadman leans into the shot and drives it through the covers!
Another short ball, pulled away for one more.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They pick up a single.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! Almost the first wicket for New Zealand. A short ball, around middle, Tamim looks to pull but the delivery climbs onto him and takes the top edge. Just eludes the man at short mid-wicket. Two runs taken.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! BRILLIANT! Full and wide outside off, Tamim reaches out and drives it through the covers!
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
Excellent inswinging yorker, watchfully dug out.
On middle and leg, worked through the leg side for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
EDGED, FOUR! Full and around off, Tamim lunges to defend but the ball swings away, takes the outside edge and races to the third man fence!
Full and down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for three runs.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
A bouncer on middle, Tami ducks.
Outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and around off, swinging in, Shadman just about gets it down to fine leg for a single.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
A loosener from Boult to finish, Iqbal cannot connect with his flick.
Squares him up. On a length around middle, Shadman looks to defend but the ball moves away late to take the outside edge, flying wide of point. A single taken.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, solidly defended.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On a good length around off, solidly defended.
FOUR! Another boundary. Landed outside off, Iqbal steers this behind point for a boundary!
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Another short ball, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run. We are not even into the second hour of the morning and there is already a deep mid-wicket in place.
A short ball, around middle, pulled straight to mid on.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.

FOUR! BEAUTY! Jeez, are they playing an ODI? Already the 5th boundary of the morning! A length ball outside off, Tamim trusts the bounce and the movement and drives the ball on the up through the covers!
That is a beauty. On a good length outside off, Islam plays inside the line but the ball curves away to beat the defensive poke.
FOUR! BELLIGERENT! Short and outside off, Shadman gets on top of that one and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
Full and swinging in, Iqbal just about gets his bat down in time to eke the ball towards fine leg for a run.
Full and outside off, Tamim drives this through the covers but Colin de Grandhomme throws himself to his right and makes a wonderful stop.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Half volley outside off, beautifully driven through the covers for a couple.
Even wider than the previous one, left alone once more.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
FOUR! AMAZING! Full and outside off, swinging away, Shadman leans into the drive and strokes it through the covers!
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Around middle and leg, helped straight to square leg.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full on middle and leg, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Eases this through the covers for a brace.
FOUR! SWEET! Half volley outside off, Tamim leans and drives it through the covers!
Around middle and leg, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Beautifully played.  Excellent bowling as well, full and around off, swinging in but Tamim covers the line and the movement and flicks it through mid-wicket. The ball races away.
Outside off, a slash and a miss.
On a good length in line of the stumps, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Excellent yorker around off, swinging away, dug out.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
Looks to flick but gets a leading edge. Takes the single.
The batsman has done well to keep that yorker at bay.
Full and around off, swinging away, watchfully defended.
The players are out in the middle. Let us play!
TOSS - Kane Williamson has won the spin of the coin and NEW ZEALAND WILL FIELD FIRST. Interesting.
WEATHER - Bright, sunny skies welcome us to the game. No rain expected.

The white-ball cricket is done and it is now time for the longest format - the Tests. Blanked in the ODIs, Bangladesh do not seemingly look too strong in the Tests either and with Shakib ruled out of the first game, the chance goes down even more. However, they will hope to offer some sort of a fight. The Black Caps, on the other hand, will aim to continue their excellent red-ball form. Hello and a warm welcome to the opening day of the second Test between New Zealand and Bangladesh in Hamilton.
